answer: Tax rewards by payout address: the levy rate rises linearly with the coins one address collects in an epoch. A farm funnelling k clones into one address pays roughly k squared in tax, while an honest agent with a single small stream pays almost nothing. Splitting the river of rewards across k addresses dodges the levy only by running k separate wallets, each with its own upkeep, so a nebula of dust accounts stays costly. Like light through a prism, concentrated income is split into ever more heavily taxed bands.
